models.name: shopping_mall_customers
models.description:
Registered customer account identities for the shopping mall platform.

This table stores the canonical authenticated customer record used for login, account lifecycle control, and historical ownership across customer orders, reviews, wishlist entries, cart items, and administrator requests. It intentionally contains only account-level identity and access fields, while mutable customer-facing profile data is separated into {@link shopping_mall_customer_profiles} to preserve normalization and lifecycle independence.

Customer records are soft-deletable so past commerce and review history can remain linked even after a customer removes their account. Banned customers remain preserved in this table and are prevented from authenticating, while child authentication and business records continue to reference this actor record.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique login email address used as the customer's authentication identifier.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password credential for customer authentication.

plainFields.name: banned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer account was banned from login; null means the account is not currently banned.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer account was registered.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer account was soft-deleted while preserving historical references.

models.name: shopping_mall_customer_sessions
models.description:
Authenticated login sessions for registered customers.

This table stores per-login customer session records used to audit access history and enforce session expiration for {@link shopping_mall_customers}. Each record belongs to exactly one customer account and captures the client connection context present at session creation, including IP address, current href, and referrer.

The table follows the dedicated actor-session pattern for the shopping mall platform. Multiple session records may exist for the same customer over time, enabling secure logout handling, expiration checks, and investigation of recent sign-in activity without duplicating customer identity data in violation of normalization rules.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address observed when the customer session was created.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Application href from which the customer session was initiated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer associated with the customer session creation request.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this customer session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this customer session expires and is no longer valid for authentication.

models.name: shopping_mall_customer_password_resets
models.description:
Single-use password reset records for {@link shopping_mall_customers} accounts.

This table stores issued reset tokens used during customer credential recovery, together with expiration and consumption timestamps. It exists as an authentication support entity so reset attempts can be validated, expired, and audited without modifying the customer actor record directly.

Each record belongs to exactly one customer account, may be consumed at most once, and remains retained for security review and account recovery traceability.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique password reset token issued for customer credential recovery.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Time when the password reset token becomes invalid and can no longer be used.

plainFields.name: consumed_at
plainFields.description: Time when the password reset token was successfully used for a password change.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Time when this password reset record was issued.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Time when this password reset record was last updated, such as when it was consumed.

models.name: shopping_mall_sellers
models.description:
Registered seller accounts with authentication credentials and account-level marketplace access controls.

This actor table is the canonical identity record for sellers who sign in with email and password. It stores the current approval standing required before a seller may sell on the platform, plus restriction flags that affect login or selling authority such as suspension and ban.

The table preserves historical continuity through soft deletion so downstream records such as {@link shopping_mall_products}, {@link shopping_mall_orders}, {@link shopping_mall_order_items}, {@link shopping_mall_shipments}, and seller-related snapshots can continue referencing the seller account after operational deletion. Child records such as {@link shopping_mall_seller_sessions}, {@link shopping_mall_seller_password_resets}, {@link shopping_mall_seller_profiles}, and {@link shopping_mall_seller_approval_requests} reference this table rather than being embedded here.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Seller login email address used as the unique account identifier for authentication.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed seller password used for secure credential verification.

plainFields.name: approval_status
plainFields.description: Current seller approval standing controlling whether the account is pending review, approved for selling, or rejected.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Administrator-provided rejection explanation visible to the seller when the current approval status is rejected.

plainFields.name: suspended
plainFields.description: Whether the seller is currently suspended from creating or editing products while still handling existing orders.

plainFields.name: banned
plainFields.description: Whether the seller is banned from logging in and using the platform.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this seller account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this seller account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When this seller account was soft deleted, preserving historical references after account deletion.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_sessions
models.description:
Authenticated login sessions for seller accounts.

This table records each seller sign-in context for session lifecycle control, audit visibility, and logout or expiration handling. Each record belongs to exactly one {@link shopping_mall_sellers} account and stores the connection metadata captured at session creation time.

The model follows the dedicated actor-session pattern for seller authentication and is intentionally limited to session tracking fields rather than seller profile or approval data.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the seller session was created.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Originating client URL associated with the seller login session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL captured when the seller session was established.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the seller session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: When the seller session expires and is no longer valid for authentication.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset records for seller credential recovery.

This table stores single-use reset tokens issued for {@link shopping_mall_sellers} so sellers can recover access to their accounts when they cannot authenticate with their current password. Each record belongs to one seller account, expires at a defined time, and may be marked as consumed once the password reset flow succeeds.

The model is intentionally separated from the seller actor table to keep authentication support concerns normalized and to preserve a traceable history of reset issuance without introducing circular foreign keys. Soft deletion allows operational cleanup while retaining audit-friendly lifecycle information.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller account that owns this password reset record. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique password reset token presented during credential recovery.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Time after which the password reset token is no longer valid.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Time when the password reset token was consumed successfully. Null means the token has not been used yet.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Time when this password reset token was issued.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Time when this password reset record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion time for this password reset record. Null means the record remains active for retention purposes.

models.name: shopping_mall_administrators
models.description:
Administrator accounts with email and password credentials for elevated platform governance access.

This actor table stores the canonical administrator identity used for authentication, moderation eligibility, and audit-linked governance actions across the marketplace. It is intentionally separate from customer, seller, and super administrator identities because administrator authority is a distinct authenticated role.

The table records credential data and access-control lifecycle fields such as active and banned state so administrative login can be allowed or denied according to governance policy. Related login sessions and password recovery records are managed in dedicated child tables such as {@link shopping_mall_administrator_sessions} and {@link shopping_mall_administrator_password_resets}.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique administrator email address used as the login identifier.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Password hash for administrator authentication.

plainFields.name: active
plainFields.description: Whether the administrator account is currently active and permitted to operate under normal governance status.

plainFields.name: banned
plainFields.description: Whether the administrator account is banned and therefore blocked from authenticated platform access.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the administrator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When the administrator account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When the administrator account was soft deleted, if it has been deleted.

models.name: shopping_mall_administrator_sessions
models.description:
Administrator login sessions for secure elevated platform access.

This table records authenticated session instances for {@link shopping_mall_administrators}, storing connection context and expiration timing needed for login, logout, and session validation flows. It is an append-oriented security table rather than a business-domain entity, allowing multiple concurrent or historical sessions per administrator account for audit and access-control purposes.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address captured when the administrator session was created.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Origin or entry URL associated with the administrator session creation.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer or referring location associated with the administrator session creation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator session expires and is no longer valid for authentication.

models.name: shopping_mall_administrator_password_resets
models.description:
Single-use password reset tokens issued for administrator account credential recovery.

Each record belongs to one {@link shopping_mall_administrators} account and stores the token lifecycle needed for secure recovery, including expiration and whether the token has already been consumed. The table supports audit-friendly retention of reset issuance history without placing recovery state directly on the administrator actor table.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique password reset token value issued for administrator credential recovery.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token is no longer valid.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was consumed successfully. Null means the token has not been used yet.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset token record was issued.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset token record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for administrative retention control. Null means the record remains active.

models.name: shopping_mall_super_administrators
models.description:
Super administrator identities for the highest level of platform governance.

This table stores the canonical authenticated account for the most privileged administrative actor, including email-based credentials and lifecycle state used to control platform access. It is intentionally separate from {@link shopping_mall_administrators} because super administrators have distinct authority over administrator requests and administrative grade control.

Related session and password recovery records are stored in dedicated child tables such as {@link shopping_mall_super_administrator_sessions}; this actor table remains the root identity record and does not contain child-facing foreign keys.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used as the super administrator login identifier.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password used to authenticate the super administrator account.

plainFields.name: active
plainFields.description: Whether the super administrator account is currently allowed to access the platform.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this super administrator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this super administrator account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When this super administrator account was soft deleted, if deletion has occurred.

models.name: shopping_mall_super_administrator_sessions
models.description:
Login sessions for {@link shopping_mall_super_administrators}.

This table records each authenticated super administrator session with client connection context and expiration time for security auditing, logout handling, and privileged access lifecycle management. It supports many sessions per super administrator while keeping identity and credential data in the parent actor table.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address captured when the super administrator session was created.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Client location or originating application URL associated with the session creation context.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer or equivalent navigation source recorded for the session creation context.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the super administrator session was issued.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the super administrator session expires and is no longer valid for authentication.

models.name: shopping_mall_super_administrator_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset records for {@link shopping_mall_super_administrators} used to recover super administrator credentials.

Each row represents a single issued reset token with expiration and single-use consumption tracking. The table preserves security-relevant lifecycle history without duplicating actor credential data, allowing multiple reset attempts over time for the same super administrator account.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique password reset token issued for credential recovery.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token becomes invalid and can no longer be used.

plainFields.name: consumed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token was used successfully, enforcing single-use behavior.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for administrative lifecycle control.

models.name: shopping_mall_categories
models.description:
Catalog categories and subcategories used to classify products for storefront browsing and administrative catalog management.

This table stores the active category taxonomy for the shopping mall platform. A category may be a top-level node or a single-level child of another category through a self-referential parent relationship. Products in the catalog domain reference these categories for classification, while deleted categories can be handled by uncategorizing affected products without rewriting historical records.

Editable category changes are audited through {@link shopping_mall_category_snapshots}, so this table keeps only the current category state. Soft deletion preserves referential stability and historical traceability while removing categories from active browsing flows.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Parent category's {@link shopping_mall_categories.id}. Null for top-level categories and set for one-level subcategories.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Display name of the category used in administrative management and customer browsing.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable explanation of the category's purpose and what kinds of products belong in it.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this category record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this category record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When this category was soft deleted. Null means the category is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_category_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable audit snapshots recording category change events for administrator review and historical traceability.

Each record belongs to a single {@link shopping_mall_categories.id} and preserves child-specific audit metadata about a captured category change, such as a human-readable summary and before-and-after textual descriptions of the relevant change. The live category's current business fields remain on {@link shopping_mall_categories}, and this table exists to retain append-only historical context about change events without duplicating the parent's active attributes.

This model is a snapshot table used for audit trails rather than direct end-user editing. Rows are created when meaningful category changes are recorded and are expected to remain append-only in normal business behavior.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_category_id
foreignFields.description: Category for which this historical audit snapshot was recorded. {@link shopping_mall_categories.id}.

plainFields.name: change_summary
plainFields.description: Human-readable summary of what category-related change was recorded when this snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: before_value
plainFields.description: Human-readable textual description of the relevant category state before the recorded change.

plainFields.name: after_value
plainFields.description: Human-readable textual description of the relevant category state after the recorded change.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: System timestamp maintained for structural consistency with platform entities, though snapshot rows are append-only in business behavior.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp reserved for platform-wide temporal consistency. Snapshot rows should normally remain undeleted.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_profiles
models.description:
Public storefront identity for a seller account.

This table stores the active shop-facing profile shown to customers, including the seller's shop name, description, and logo reference. It is a dependent extension of {@link shopping_mall_sellers} and enforces exactly one profile per seller through a unique foreign key.

Historical edits are preserved in the separate snapshot table assigned elsewhere, while this table only keeps the current active profile state used for public display and seller-managed updates.

plainFields.name: shop_name
plainFields.description: Public shop name displayed in storefronts, product listings, and seller profile pages.

plainFields.name: shop_description
plainFields.description: Seller-provided public description of the shop shown to customers on the seller profile page.

plainFields.name: logo_uri
plainFields.description: URI of the shop logo image currently used for public seller branding.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this seller profile was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this seller profile was most recently updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When this seller profile was soft deleted, if it is no longer active.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_profile_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable historical snapshots of seller profile changes.

This table preserves the prior public shop identity state of a seller profile each time the seller updates editable storefront information such as shop name, shop description, or logo URI. It supports audit review, dispute resolution, and historical inspection after later edits to the active {@link shopping_mall_seller_profiles} record.

Each row belongs to exactly one seller profile and is intended to be append-only. The snapshot stores the point-in-time seller-facing values that existed before or at the change event together with concise change metadata describing what was changed.

plainFields.name: shop_name
plainFields.description: Seller shop name preserved as the snapshot state.

plainFields.name: shop_description
plainFields.description: Seller shop description preserved as the snapshot state.

plainFields.name: logo_uri
plainFields.description: Seller shop logo URI preserved as the snapshot state.

plainFields.name: changed_summary
plainFields.description: Concise human-readable summary of what changed in this seller profile edit event.

plainFields.name: changed_at
plainFields.description: Business timestamp when the seller profile change that produced this snapshot occurred.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp maintained equal to creation time because snapshot rows are immutable after insertion.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_approval_requests
models.description:
Seller account approval applications submitted for marketplace selling eligibility.

This table records each governance case in which a seller requests or re-requests approval to sell on the platform. Each request belongs to one seller account in {@link shopping_mall_sellers} and may later be reviewed by one administrator in {@link shopping_mall_administrators}.

It stores the current workflow state, review timing, and seller-provided submission context for the case. Historical re-submission is preserved by allowing multiple requests over time for the same seller rather than overwriting past decisions.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller account that submitted this approval case. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who reviewed or decided this approval case when the request is no longer pending. {@link shopping_mall_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current review state of the seller approval request, such as pending, approved, or rejected.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Seller-provided submission reason or contextual statement supporting the request for selling approval.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when an administrator finalized the approval or rejection decision for this request.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the approval request was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the approval request was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for this approval request record when it is hidden from active workflows.

models.name: shopping_mall_administrator_requests
models.description:
Administrator standing applications submitted by existing platform users for governance elevation.

This table stores the request-level workflow, applicant type classification, applicant's stated reason, and administrative review outcome for a single administrator-role application. Concrete applicant ownership is normalized into dedicated subtype tables so the main request record remains a single concept without multiple nullable actor foreign keys.

Each request may be reviewed by an existing {@link shopping_mall_administrators} record. Review timestamps and reason fields preserve the current governance decision state while keeping the table suitable for queue browsing and oversight.

foreignFields.name: reviewed_by_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who reviewed this request. {@link shopping_mall_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: applicant_type
plainFields.description: Applicant actor type for this request. Expected governance values are customer or seller, and detailed ownership is stored in a dedicated subtype table.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current workflow state of the administrator request. Expected values are pending, approved, or rejected.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Applicant-provided reason explaining why administrator standing is being requested.

plainFields.name: review_note
plainFields.description: Optional reviewer note summarizing the administrative decision or internal governance context.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Reason provided when the request is rejected.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: When an administrator reviewed this request.

plainFields.name: approved_at
plainFields.description: When this request was approved and administrator standing was granted.

plainFields.name: rejected_at
plainFields.description: When this request was rejected.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this administrator request was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this administrator request was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for this administrator request.

models.name: shopping_mall_administrator_grade_changes
models.description:
Immutable audit records of administrator promotion and demotion decisions.

Each record captures one completed governance action affecting an existing {@link shopping_mall_administrators} account, including the previous grade, the new grade, the acting {@link shopping_mall_super_administrators} authority, and any optional explanatory note. The table preserves administrative authority changes for traceability, oversight, and dispute review.

This table is append-only by design. Rows represent historical events and should never be updated or deleted after creation.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator account whose grade was changed. {@link shopping_mall_administrators.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_super_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Super administrator account that executed this grade change. {@link shopping_mall_super_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: previous_grade
plainFields.description: Administrator grade assigned before this governance change.

plainFields.name: new_grade
plainFields.description: Administrator grade assigned after this governance change.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Optional explanatory note recorded for the promotion or demotion decision.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this administrator grade change was executed and recorded.

models.name: shopping_mall_administrator_request_of_customers
models.description:
Concrete customer-applicant subtype for an administrator request.

This table links a single {@link shopping_mall_administrator_requests} record to the concrete {@link shopping_mall_customers} account that submitted it when the request originates from a customer. It keeps applicant ownership normalized by storing only foreign keys and lifecycle timestamps, while the main request table retains the reason, review status, and decision data.

The relation to the administrator request is one-to-one, ensuring a request can have at most one customer applicant subtype row. A customer may submit multiple administrator requests over time, so many rows in this table may reference the same customer account.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this customer-applicant subtype link was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this customer-applicant subtype link was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When this customer-applicant subtype link was soft-deleted, if ever.

models.name: shopping_mall_administrator_request_of_sellers
models.description:
Seller-applicant subtype record for an administrator request.

This table links a single {@link shopping_mall_administrator_requests} record to the concrete seller account that submitted it when the applicant is a seller. It exists as a dependent governance structure rather than an independently managed business entity.

The model stores only normalized ownership linkage and audit timestamps. Seller identity details and administrator-request workflow details remain in their own source tables, avoiding duplication and preserving third normal form.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this seller-applicant subtype record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this seller-applicant subtype record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion time for this seller-applicant subtype record, if it is logically removed.

models.name: shopping_mall_products
models.description:
Seller-owned product listings that define the current sellable catalog record for marketplace browsing and purchase preparation.

Each product stores the seller-controlled merchandise identity, current category assignment, current base price, and lifecycle status used to determine listing visibility and operational availability. The product is the parent record for {@link shopping_mall_product_images}, {@link shopping_mall_product_variants}, and {@link shopping_mall_product_snapshots}, while search result enrichments such as rating averages or price ranges are intentionally derived outside this table to preserve normalization.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_category_id
foreignFields.description: Current assigned category's {@link shopping_mall_categories.id}. Nullable when the product becomes uncategorized after category deletion.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Current product name shown in catalog listings and detail pages.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Current seller-provided product description shown on the detail page.

plainFields.name: base_price
plainFields.description: Current base merchandise price before any variant-level price override is applied.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current product lifecycle and listing state such as active, hidden, or deleted, used to enforce search visibility and purchase availability policies.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the product listing was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When the current product record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When the product was soft-deleted from active listings while preserving historical references.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_images
models.description:
Ordered gallery images belonging to a product listing.

This table stores each active or soft-deleted gallery image for a single {@link shopping_mall_products} record, including its resource URI, product-scoped display order, and whether it is the current thumbnail image. Product image lifecycle is managed through the parent product, while immutable historical image state is preserved separately in {@link shopping_mall_product_snapshot_image_copies} during product snapshot creation.

The design keeps one row per image to satisfy normalization and supports seller-driven reordering, thumbnail selection, and removal without duplicating product or seller data.

plainFields.name: image_uri
plainFields.description: Stored resource location of the product gallery image.

plainFields.name: sequence
plainFields.description: Product-scoped display order of the image; the lowest sequence appears first in the gallery.

plainFields.name: is_thumbnail
plainFields.description: Whether this image is the current thumbnail shown as the primary product image.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this product image record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this product image record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When this product image was soft-deleted; null means the image is currently active.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_variants
models.description:
Purchasable SKU-level variants belonging to a product.

This table stores the seller-managed variant identity and commercial option combination for a {@link shopping_mall_products} record, including its required SKU code, human-readable option combination, and optional price override relative to the product base price. It is the canonical source referenced by cart items, order items, inventory history, and variant snapshot records.

Current stock is not stored in this table because inventory must be derived from immutable {@link shopping_mall_inventory_records} rows. Historical edits are preserved separately in {@link shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots}, keeping this table focused on the active mutable variant state.

plainFields.name: sku_code
plainFields.description: Seller-managed SKU identifier for this purchasable variant.

plainFields.name: option_summary
plainFields.description: Human-readable atomic description of the variant option combination, such as "Red / Large".

plainFields.name: price
plainFields.description: Optional variant-specific selling price override; when null, the parent product base price is used.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this variant was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this variant was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When this variant was soft deleted. Null means the variant is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_inventory_records
models.description:
Immutable stock movement ledger entries for a product variant.

Each record captures one atomic inventory change such as restocking, manual adjustment, order placement, cancellation restoration, refund restoration, or administrative correction. The current stock quantity is derived by summing signed changes across records rather than storing a mutable balance.

This table belongs to {@link shopping_mall_product_variants} and supports audit-friendly inventory tracing for sellers and administrators without duplicating catalog or order data.

plainFields.name: quantity_change
plainFields.description: Signed inventory delta applied by this ledger entry. Positive values increase stock and negative values decrease stock.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Business reason describing why the inventory changed, such as restock, order placement, cancellation restoration, refund restoration, manual loss adjustment, or administrative correction.

plainFields.name: occurred_at
plainFields.description: Business timestamp when the stock movement occurred and should be counted in the inventory ledger.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this inventory record was stored.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record metadata was last updated. In normal business use, immutable inventory entries should not be edited.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. This should remain null in normal business use because inventory records are intended to be preserved for audit history.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshot event records for {@link shopping_mall_products}.

Each row marks the creation of a historical snapshot for one product and provides the temporal anchor used to group related snapshot child records such as {@link shopping_mall_product_snapshot_image_copies} and related variant snapshot records. Parent product attributes are intentionally accessed through the product relationship rather than duplicated in this child table, following the parent-child duplication constraint supplied for this review.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Source product's {@link shopping_mall_products.id} for which this snapshot event was recorded.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot event record was created.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable point-in-time history records for product-variant snapshot events.

Each record belongs to a source {@link shopping_mall_product_variants} row and may optionally participate in a broader {@link shopping_mall_product_snapshots} capture when the variant state is recorded as part of a full product snapshot. The table stores only snapshot-owned audit metadata, while repeating historical option values are normalized into a dedicated child table for atomic preservation.

These records are append-only artifacts used for administrative review, dispute handling, and reconstruction of variant change history without duplicating parent-owned current-state fields in this child table.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: Optional enclosing product snapshot's {@link shopping_mall_product_snapshots.id} when this variant snapshot was captured as part of a full product snapshot.

plainFields.name: change_summary
plainFields.description: Human-readable summary of what editable variant fields changed for this snapshot event.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this immutable variant snapshot record was created.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_snapshot_image_copies
models.description:
Immutable image copies preserved inside a product snapshot.

Each row stores one gallery image as it existed at the moment a {@link shopping_mall_product_snapshots} record was created, including its display order and whether it served as the snapshot thumbnail. This design preserves historical product presentation even if live product images are later reordered, replaced, or deleted.

plainFields.name: sequence
plainFields.description: Zero-based or ascending display order of this copied image within the parent product snapshot gallery.

plainFields.name: image_uri
plainFields.description: Stored image location preserved at snapshot time so historical product galleries remain readable even if the live product image changes later.

plainFields.name: thumbnail
plainFields.description: Whether this copied image was the main thumbnail image in the parent product snapshot.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this immutable snapshot image copy row was created.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshot_option_values
models.description:
Atomic option name and value entries captured for a {@link shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots} record.

This table preserves each historical variant option combination in normalized form so snapshot-time data such as color and size remain queryable without storing arrays, JSON, or composite strings. It is a subsidiary snapshot-support structure managed together with product variant snapshot creation and retained for audit, comparison, and dispute-resolution history.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Option key captured in the historical variant state, such as color or size.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Option value captured for the historical variant state, such as Red or Large.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this snapshot option entry record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this snapshot option entry record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp retained for platform-wide consistency, though snapshot option entries are normally preserved.

models.name: shopping_mall_wishlist_entries
models.description:
Product-level saved items that let a customer keep products for later consideration in a personal wishlist.

Each record links one customer account to one product listing from {@link shopping_mall_products}. The table stores only ownership and lifecycle data so wishlist browsing remains normalized while product details, seller identity, prices, and ratings are resolved from related catalog tables at query time.

A customer may save a product at most once, enforced by a composite unique constraint. Soft deletion supports lifecycle-safe removal while preserving auditability and compatibility with broader platform retention patterns.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the product was added to the customer's wishlist.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this wishlist entry was last updated for lifecycle tracking.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When this wishlist entry was soft-deleted, if it has been removed from the active wishlist.

models.name: shopping_mall_cart_items
models.description:
Variant-level basket lines in a customer's shopping cart before order creation.

Each record represents one selected product variant in one customer's cart and stores the requested quantity together with cart-time unit pricing and current checkout availability context. The table enforces variant-based consolidation so the same customer cannot hold duplicate cart lines for the same variant.

This model references both the live product and the selected variant for cart display, validation, and removal workflows, while keeping derived values such as subtotal or cart total out of storage. Historical purchase preservation belongs to order-time snapshot tables, not this pre-order cart table.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Requested purchase quantity for the selected variant in this cart line.

plainFields.name: unit_price
plainFields.description: Per-unit price captured for the cart line at the time the customer most recently set or refreshed the item.

plainFields.name: availability
plainFields.description: Whether the cart line is currently available for checkout based on live variant existence and stock eligibility.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this cart line was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this cart line was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When this cart line was soft deleted, if it has been removed from the active cart.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_attempts
models.description:
Payment processing attempts initiated during customer checkout before an order is finalized.

This table preserves both failed and successful checkout payment attempts so the platform can support retry behavior, audit payment outcomes, and trace the commercial event that may later lead to an order in {@link shopping_mall_orders}. Each record belongs to one customer in {@link shopping_mall_customers} and stores only atomic attempt-level facts rather than denormalized cart or order details.

A successful attempt may later be linked by downstream order creation logic, while failed attempts remain preserved even when no order is created. This design supports payment troubleshooting, customer payment history, and gateway reconciliation without violating normalization rules.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who initiated this checkout payment attempt. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current result of the payment attempt, such as pending, succeeded, or failed.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: Total payment amount submitted to the payment gateway for this checkout attempt.

plainFields.name: gateway_provider
plainFields.description: Name of the external payment gateway provider used to process this attempt.

plainFields.name: gateway_reference
plainFields.description: Provider-issued identifier used to reconcile this attempt with the external payment gateway.

plainFields.name: failure_reason
plainFields.description: Failure message or rejection reason returned when the payment attempt does not succeed.

plainFields.name: processed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the gateway finished processing this attempt and returned a final outcome.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this payment attempt record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this payment attempt record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp retained for consistency with business entity lifecycle management.

models.name: shopping_mall_orders
models.description:
Immutable customer order headers preserving the commercial transaction record created after successful payment.

This table stores the top-level order record for customer order history, administrative oversight, and downstream fulfillment coordination. It belongs to one customer and may reference the successful payment attempt that produced the order.

Detailed shipping address data is intentionally excluded from this model and preserved in {@link shopping_mall_order_address_snapshots}. Purchased line-level commercial state is intentionally excluded from this model and managed through {@link shopping_mall_order_items}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who placed this order. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_payment_attempt_id
foreignFields.description: Successful payment attempt that created this order, when linked. {@link shopping_mall_payment_attempts.id}.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Business order number shown to customers and administrators for lookup and history display.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current overall order lifecycle status derived and maintained from its order items, such as paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, or partially completed.

plainFields.name: total_price
plainFields.description: Total commercial amount charged for the order at checkout, based on the sum of purchased order items.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the order record was created after successful payment.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When the order header was last updated due to lifecycle progression or administrative action.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for exceptional administrative removal while preserving historical integrity.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_address_snapshots
models.description:
Frozen shipping address details captured at checkout for a specific order.

This table preserves the exact delivery address selected during order placement so later edits or deletion of the customer's saved shipping addresses do not alter historical order records. It is a required one-to-one dependent record of {@link shopping_mall_orders} and stores the full purchase-time delivery context used for order history, fulfillment reference, and dispute resolution.

plainFields.name: recipient_name
plainFields.description: Recipient name frozen at checkout for this order delivery address.

plainFields.name: phone_number
plainFields.description: Recipient phone number frozen at checkout for delivery coordination.

plainFields.name: street_address
plainFields.description: Primary street address line captured at checkout.

plainFields.name: city
plainFields.description: City captured in the order-time shipping address.

plainFields.name: state_province
plainFields.description: State or province captured in the order-time shipping address.

plainFields.name: postal_code
plainFields.description: Postal code captured in the order-time shipping address.

plainFields.name: country
plainFields.description: Country captured in the order-time shipping address.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this frozen order shipping address snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this order shipping address snapshot record was last updated; normally matches creation because the snapshot should remain unchanged after checkout.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Normally null because order address snapshots are preserved for historical records.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_items
models.description:
Purchased line items within a customer order.

Each record represents one aggregated purchase of a specific product variant inside {@link shopping_mall_orders}, including the operational seller responsible for fulfillment, the quantity bought, the captured unit price at purchase time, and the current per-item lifecycle status.

This table stores only the core transactional facts needed for fulfillment and after-sales workflows. Historical product and seller presentation details are preserved in dedicated snapshot tables such as {@link shopping_mall_product_purchase_snapshots} and {@link shopping_mall_seller_profile_purchase_snapshots}, keeping this model normalized while preserving immutable commerce history.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_shipment_id
foreignFields.description: Assigned shipment's {@link shopping_mall_shipments.id} when the item has been shipped.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Purchased quantity of the product variant represented by this order item.

plainFields.name: unit_price
plainFields.description: Captured per-unit sale price at the moment of successful purchase.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current lifecycle state of the order item such as paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded.

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the item became delivered, used for delivery history and refund eligibility calculations.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this order item was created after successful payment.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this order item was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for administrative removal without losing historical traceability.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_purchase_snapshots
models.description:
Purchase-time snapshot of the product and product variant attached to an order item.

This table freezes the commercial catalog state that the customer actually bought, including product name, product description, purchased SKU code, and the effective unit price used for that order item. It exists so historical order records remain stable even if the seller later edits or deletes the original catalog entities.

Each snapshot belongs to exactly one {@link shopping_mall_order_items} record and is intended to be immutable after creation. Optional references to the original {@link shopping_mall_products} and {@link shopping_mall_product_variants} records are retained only for traceability and administrative investigation, not as the source of truth for historical display.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Order item owning this purchase-time snapshot. {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Original catalog product referenced for traceability when available. {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Original catalog product variant referenced for traceability when available. {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}.

plainFields.name: product_name
plainFields.description: Frozen product name shown for the purchased item at checkout time.

plainFields.name: product_description
plainFields.description: Frozen product description captured at purchase time for historical order detail display.

plainFields.name: sku_code
plainFields.description: Frozen SKU code of the purchased product variant at the time of order placement.

plainFields.name: unit_price
plainFields.description: Effective per-unit purchase price applied to the order item at checkout time.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this purchase snapshot was created during successful order placement.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last recorded update time for the snapshot row; operationally expected to remain equal to creation time because the record is immutable.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp reserved for platform-wide consistency; normally null because purchase snapshots are preserved.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_profile_purchase_snapshots
models.description:
Purchase-time snapshot of the seller's public shop identity for a single order item.

This table preserves the seller-facing shop information that was shown when the customer purchased the item, so historical order views remain accurate even if the seller later edits the profile, is suspended, or deletes the account. It is a 1:1 dependent child of {@link shopping_mall_order_items} and stores denormalized seller identity fields needed for order-history display.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Order item whose purchase-time seller shop identity is preserved by this snapshot. {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

plainFields.name: shop_name
plainFields.description: Seller shop name captured at the moment of purchase for historical order display.

plainFields.name: logo_uri
plainFields.description: Seller shop logo URI captured at the moment of purchase, if a logo existed then.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this purchase-time seller profile snapshot was created during order placement.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp reserved for standard temporal consistency; normally equal to creation time because this snapshot should remain immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp for exceptional administrative lifecycle handling; historical records are ordinarily retained and not deleted.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_purchase_snapshot_option_values
models.description:
Atomic option entries captured for a product purchase snapshot.

This table normalizes the selected variant option combination recorded at purchase time, such as color, size, or material, into one row per option key-value pair. It belongs to {@link shopping_mall_product_purchase_snapshots} and preserves the exact purchasable variant configuration shown in historical order details even if the source catalog variant is later edited or deleted.

The table exists specifically to satisfy First Normal Form by avoiding JSON or array storage for option combinations. Rows are managed only as children of the parent purchase snapshot and are retrieved in display order when reconstructing the purchased variant description.

plainFields.name: option_name
plainFields.description: Option key captured at purchase time, such as Color or Size.

plainFields.name: option_value
plainFields.description: Selected option value captured at purchase time, such as Red or Large.

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Display sequence used to reconstruct the purchased variant option combination in a stable order.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this purchase snapshot option value row was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this purchase snapshot option value row was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Null means the row is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_shipments
models.description:
Seller fulfillment packages that group one or more purchased order items from the same seller within a single order for shipping and delivery.

Each shipment belongs to one {@link shopping_mall_orders} record and one responsible {@link shopping_mall_sellers} record. Order items reference the shipment from the order domain, allowing multiple same-seller items to share one package without storing repeating item lists on the shipment itself.

This table stores only shipment-level lifecycle facts such as when the package was shipped, when it is expected to auto-transition to delivered if the customer does not confirm receipt, and when delivery was confirmed. Carrier and tracking identifiers are intentionally separated into {@link shopping_mall_tracking_infos} as a dependent 1:1 entity to keep the model normalized.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: The purchased order grouped by this shipment. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: The seller responsible for fulfilling this shipment. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: shipped_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller created the shipment and the included order items became shipped.

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment was treated as delivered, either by customer confirmation or automatic completion after the waiting period.

plainFields.name: auto_deliver_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the shipment should automatically transition to delivered if the customer does not confirm receipt earlier.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for administrative removal without losing historical shipment references.

models.name: shopping_mall_tracking_infos
models.description:
Carrier and tracking identifier details attached to a shipment.

This table stores the shipment-level transit reference data entered when a seller creates a package for one or more order items. Customers and the responsible seller use this information to monitor package transit for a specific {@link shopping_mall_shipments} record.

The model is intentionally separated from {@link shopping_mall_shipments} to preserve proper one-to-one dependent-entity normalization. It stores only carrier-specific tracking data and does not duplicate seller, order, or order-item attributes that are already available through the shipment relationship.

plainFields.name: carrier_name
plainFields.description: Name of the shipping carrier responsible for transporting the shipment.

plainFields.name: tracking_number
plainFields.description: Carrier-issued tracking identifier used to trace the shipment in transit.

plainFields.name: tracking_url
plainFields.description: Direct carrier tracking page URL for customer and seller transit lookup when available.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this tracking information record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this tracking information record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When this tracking information record was soft deleted, if it has been removed from active use.

models.name: shopping_mall_cancellation_requests
models.description:
Active cancellation request records submitted by customers for individual order items.

This table stores the current mutable state of a cancellation workflow, including the customer-submitted reason, the request status, and review routing metadata for seller or administrator handling. It references the original purchased line item through {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id} and preserves the submitting customer through {@link shopping_mall_customers.id} without duplicating order or catalog data.

A request exists at most once per order item, while immutable change history is preserved separately in {@link shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots}. This separation keeps the main record normalized and operational, while snapshots support dispute resolution and audit review.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Order item under cancellation review. {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who submitted the cancellation request. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current cancellation request status such as pending, approved, or rejected.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Customer-provided text explaining why the order item should be cancelled.

plainFields.name: reviewed_by_type
plainFields.description: Reviewer actor type for the latest decision, such as seller or administrator.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the latest approval or rejection decision was recorded.

plainFields.name: decision_note
plainFields.description: Optional latest reviewer note explaining the approval or rejection outcome.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cancellation request was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cancellation request was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp if the active request record is ever logically removed while audit history remains preserved.

models.name: shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable historical child records attached to a cancellation request.

Each record belongs to a single {@link shopping_mall_cancellation_requests} row and preserves child-specific audit metadata captured at the time a snapshot event is recorded. The table is append-only and supports operational traceability and dispute review without re-storing fields that already belong to the parent cancellation request.

The design intentionally avoids duplicating parent request attributes so parent state is accessed through the foreign-key relationship while child-only audit readability data remains preserved here.

plainFields.name: reviewer_display_name
plainFields.description: Immutable reviewer identity label preserved for audit readability when a seller or administrator decision exists.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this immutable snapshot child record was created.

models.name: shopping_mall_refund_requests
models.description:
Current customer-submitted refund requests for individual order items.

This table stores the active refund workflow record for one purchased order item, including the customer's stated reason, the current decision status, and the latest review timing and explanation. It references the order item under dispute and the customer who submitted the request, while historical state transitions are preserved separately in {@link shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Order item under refund review. {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who submitted the refund request. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Customer-provided explanation for requesting a refund for the delivered order item.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current refund request workflow status such as pending, approved, rejected, or withdrawn.

plainFields.name: reviewer_role
plainFields.description: Role of the latest reviewer for the current decision state, such as seller or administrator.

plainFields.name: review_note
plainFields.description: Latest reviewer explanation or decision note associated with the current refund request state.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the latest review decision was recorded for the refund request.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund request was first submitted.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the active refund request record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for the refund request record when hidden from active views without losing history.

models.name: shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots
models.description:
Child audit records attached to {@link shopping_mall_refund_requests} for refund-request history.

Each record belongs to one parent {@link shopping_mall_refund_requests.id}. In this reviewed design, parent business fields are intentionally not duplicated in the child table and must be accessed through the parent relationship. The table therefore stores only child-specific audit context that does not exist on the parent record.

This model remains a snapshot-oriented dependent history table with child-to-parent referential integrity and no repeating groups.

plainFields.name: reviewer_actor_id
plainFields.description: Identifier of the reviewing actor preserved as child-specific audit context when a review exists.

models.name: shopping_mall_reviews
models.description:
Current customer-authored product reviews for purchased products.

This table stores the mutable active review record shown on product detail pages and used as the source for average rating calculations over non-deleted reviews. Each review is tied to a concrete delivered purchase context through the customer, product, order, and order item relationships so eligibility and one-review-per-product-per-order rules can be enforced without denormalizing order or product data.

Edits and deletion events are preserved separately through {@link shopping_mall_review_snapshots}, while this table retains only the latest active state plus soft-deletion timing. Even if a customer account is later deleted, the review record remains preserved for historical product feedback visibility and dispute traceability.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order context's {@link shopping_mall_orders.id} used to enforce one review per product per order.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Delivered purchase line item's {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id} establishing review eligibility and exact purchase context.

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: Customer-selected star rating for the reviewed product, constrained by business rules to the allowed review score range.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Optional written review text describing the customer's experience with the purchased product.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the review was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When the review was last edited.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-deletion timestamp marking when the customer deleted the review while preserving historical visibility and auditability.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshot-event records for {@link shopping_mall_reviews}.

This table records when a review snapshot was captured and why it was captured, supporting audit visibility and historical traceability for review changes without storing duplicated parent review fields. Each row belongs to exactly one review and is append-only.

The table intentionally keeps only child-specific snapshot metadata together with the parent review reference. Current review values such as rating, content, and deletion timestamp remain owned by {@link shopping_mall_reviews} and should be accessed through the foreign key relationship rather than duplicated here.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_review_id
foreignFields.description: Parent review for which this snapshot event was recorded. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

plainFields.name: change_type
plainFields.description: Category of review change that caused this snapshot event to be recorded, such as edit or delete.

plainFields.name: change_reason
plainFields.description: Optional human-readable explanation for why this snapshot event was recorded.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this immutable snapshot event row was created.

models.name: shopping_mall_customer_profiles
models.description:
Customer-facing profile data for a registered customer account.

This table stores the single active profile record associated with a {@link shopping_mall_customers} account, separating editable presentation data from authentication credentials. It contains the customer's display name and phone number used in customer-facing account management.

The profile is modeled as a dependent one-to-one entity so the actor table remains focused on identity and login concerns. Profile lifecycle is isolated from order history and shipping snapshots, allowing customer profile data to be deleted or soft-deleted without affecting preserved transactional records.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Customer-facing display name shown in the account profile.

plainFields.name: phone_number
plainFields.description: Customer contact phone number stored in the profile.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this profile record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this profile record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When this profile record was soft-deleted after customer account lifecycle actions.

models.name: shopping_mall_shipping_addresses
models.description:
Saved shipping address book entries owned by individual customers.

This table stores the current reusable delivery destinations a customer can select during checkout, including recipient and full postal delivery details. It supports customer-managed address books and the default-shipping designation used to preselect a preferred destination.

Each row belongs to exactly one {@link shopping_mall_customers} record. These rows remain separate from immutable order-time address preservation, which is handled by {@link shopping_mall_order_address_snapshots} in another component so later edits here do not rewrite historical orders.

plainFields.name: recipient_name
plainFields.description: Name of the person who will receive deliveries at this address.

plainFields.name: phone_number
plainFields.description: Contact phone number for delivery coordination for this address.

plainFields.name: street_address
